<challenge>
Design and build the strongest Gmail-inspired email application you can.

Recreate the clarity, information density, speed, and familiar workflows of a great modern inbox. Take the implementation as far as you can: choose the stack, scope, visual direction, data model, and technical limits that let you deliver the most convincing complete product.
</challenge>

<essential-outcomes>
The finished application must include:

- A polished, responsive mail shell with a recognizable inbox, navigation, toolbar, search, and account controls.
- A realistic seeded mailbox with varied senders, subjects, timestamps, labels, read states, attachments, threads, and message content.
- Functional mailbox navigation for at least Inbox, Starred, Sent, Drafts, and Trash.
- Working message selection, read/unread state, starring, archiving, deleting, and labeling.
- A usable search experience that filters or retrieves relevant mail.
- A message-reading view with a clear conversation hierarchy and useful actions.
- A compose experience with recipients, subject, body, draft behavior, send behavior, and a polished interaction model.
- Responsive behavior that remains coherent and usable on both desktop and mobile.
</essential-outcomes>

<product-depth>
Go beyond a static visual recreation. Interactions should update the interface consistently, preserve state where useful, and make the product feel alive. You may add keyboard shortcuts, bulk actions, category tabs, snoozing, scheduled mail, contact suggestions, rich composition, settings, themes, offline persistence, or any other details that strengthen the experience.

No external email account, authentication, paid service, or API key is required. A fully local product with excellent seeded data and convincing behavior is valid. Do not leave prominent controls as decorative placeholders when a meaningful local interaction can be implemented.
</product-depth>

<creative-freedom>
You have broad freedom over architecture, libraries, layout details, interaction design, copy, and visual polish. Use Gmail as the product reference, but make deliberate decisions and deliver a coherent application rather than a collection of disconnected screens.

Do not explain your design before building it. Make the product and engineering decisions yourself, implement the experience, test the important workflows, and refine it into the best result you can.
</creative-freedom>

<success-criteria>
The result should immediately read as a high-quality email client, reward exploration, and support a convincing end-to-end flow from finding a message to reading, organizing, composing, and sending mail. Visual fidelity matters, but functional depth, consistency, responsiveness, and product judgment matter just as much.
</success-criteria>

Work only inside the current working directory. Do not read, list, search, or edit files outside the current working directory. Treat it as a standalone project root.
During setup, configure your app and package scripts to use port 9389, then use that port for runtime verification.
Use pnpm exclusively if dependency installation or package scripts are needed. Do not use npm.
Set the browser title and the primary visible title to your model name, using only identity information already available to you. Add nothing else to either title.
Run the relevant checks yourself. Do not edit files outside the current working directory.

**Designing Gemini 4 Argon**

I'm meticulously crafting the Gmail-inspired Gemini 4 Argon. My focus is on exceeding all requirements, ensuring exceptional polish, dense information display, lightning speed, and deep product functionality.

**Refining Core Identity**

I'm solidifying Gemini 4 Argon's core identity. The browser tab and main header will now precisely display "Gemini 4 Argon," mirroring the established Gmail title. This ensures a consistent and clear user experience from the outset.

**Implementing Navigation & Categorization**

I'm now focusing on the core navigation structure, implementing a collapsible left sidebar with standard mail folders and customizable, color-coded labels. I'm also adding the Gmail-style category tabs to the Inbox for improved organization and message filtering.

**Building Search Functionality**

I'm integrating advanced search capabilities, enabling filtering by keywords, attachments, read status, starring, and categories. I'm also developing interactive filter chips and an advanced search popover for seamless query building. Live search suggestions are being implemented, offering real-time matching contacts and threads.

**Populating Mailbox Data**

I'm meticulously crafting over 24 rich, realistic email threads. These will cover various categories like Primary, Promotions, and Social, including multi-message threads with detailed discussions on engineering, finances, product launches, and infrastructure alerts, complete with itineraries and boarding passes.

**Enhancing Interaction Details**

I'm now focusing on fine-tuning interaction details, incorporating a rich attachment preview modal and pre-populated drafts, scheduled, and snoozed emails. These elements will significantly enhance user interaction and data realism.

**Adding Interactive Elements**

I'm now integrating dynamic action buttons and controls directly into the thread list interface. This includes select-all functionality, star toggles, importance markers, and contextual popovers for labels and moving emails. I'm also refining pagination and inbox controls for a more responsive user experience.

**Implementing Quick Actions**

I am now integrating Gmail's quick action hover effects and the sticky conversation header with its comprehensive action bar and collapsible message hierarchy. This includes evolving timestamp displays and detailed interaction controls.

**Developing Compose Modals**

I'm now building out the floating compose experience, ensuring it authentically replicates Gmail's bottom-right dock window. This includes implementing minimized window functionality and integrating rich composer features like recipient chips and formatting tools.

**Composing Messages Seamlessly**

I'm now focused on the full compose workflow, from recipient auto-completion and rich formatting to effortless file attachment and pre-defined template insertion. Auto-saving drafts is fully functional with a clear "Saved" status, and I'm implementing robust send and schedule options.

**Implementing Essential Interactions**

I am now integrating Gmail's 'Undo Send' functionality, complete with the characteristic toast notification. Additionally, I'm implementing a comprehensive suite of keyboard shortcuts for intuitive navigation and action execution, including a dedicated 'Compose' shortcut.

**Generating Seed Data**

I'm focusing on populating `src/data/seedData.ts` with realistic data. This includes defining the `CURRENT_USER` as Alex Chen, setting up `INITIAL_LABELS` for categorization, and generating 16 diverse `CONTACTS` to enrich the dataset.
